content: Inhaled insulin is a viable option for insulin administration and has been shown in studies to exhibit a pharmacological action comparable to that of rapid-acting insulin aspart. However, it is contraindicated for individuals with pre-existing lung diseases or for those who smoke, as these conditions may pose significant risks. Furthermore, all patients who are prescribed inhaled insulin must undergo forced expiratory volume in one second (FEV1) testing to confirm that it can be safely administered without compromising pulmonary function.
